key_insight: In pediatric first-onset nephrotic syndrome, anti-nephrin antibody levels distinguished clinical phenotypes: standard-range positivity was associated with steroid sensitivity, while high titers were enriched in steroid resistance.
clinical_relevance: Pretreatment antibody testing may help characterize pediatric nephrotic syndrome, but this study concerns kidney disease—not AI, cancer, or drug discovery.
method: Developed an automated immunoassay using modified recombinant nephrin.
Evaluated pretreatment and post-treatment antibodies in a prospective Japanese pediatric discovery cohort and an independent validation cohort.
Used immunoprecipitation–Western blotting, biopsy colocalization, and antigen inhibition for orthogonal validation.
evidence_signal: In the discovery cohort (n=103), antibodies were detected in 83/83 steroid-sensitive cases and 9/16 steroid-resistant cases; phenotype associations were also observed in the validation cohort (n=42).
watch_item: Small phenotype subgroups and the Japanese pediatric study setting limit generalizability; broader prospective validation is needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Establishment of an Anti-Nephrin Autoantibody Assay and the Predictive and Diagnostic Significance of Pre-treatment Antibody Titers in Pediatric Nephrotic Syndrome
